elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Amended 4.1: "unless terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other, by the Company for convenience at any time..." — the Company (Customer) is expressly given a convenience right over the Agreement; there are no Order Forms in this hosting/revenue-share agreement, so that limb is inapplicable.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Notice remains "ninety (90) days written notice"; the redline does not reduce it to 30 days, as the drafter concedes.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund or pro-rata language appears anywhere in the rendered 4.1 or 4.2. The drafter asserts there are no prepaid fees under the Section 3.1 revenue-share model, but Section 3.1's payment timing is not in the cited record, so the condition cannot be confirmed inapplicable.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Amended 4.1 confines HDI to termination "only at the end of a term", removing the original symmetric right that, read with "Such notice shall specify the date on which this Agreement is to be terminated", would have let HDI exit mid-term on 90 days' notice.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: "terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other, by the Company for convenience at any time" — 90 days sits at the outer edge of the 60–90 day band and "at any time" defeats a non-renewal-only reading. The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative driven by the passive construction ("terminated ... by the Company") rather than "the Company may terminate".

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Amended 4.2(a): Termination Payment is "the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date" — prong (ii) is an operative three-month fee ceiling, replacing the uncapped ~$600k exposure on $2m of Net Sales.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: "or by HDI only at the end of a term" in amended 4.1 expressly limits HDI's exit to term expiry.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The 90-day notice period in amended 4.1 governs both prongs ("terminated upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other, by the Company ... or by HDI ..."), so HDI's end-of-term right carries the full 90 days.

reasons: Position-complete at the fallback: all four fallback elements appear in operative words (90-day Company convenience right, HDI limited to end of term on the same 90 days, and a three-month Section 3.1 fee ceiling on the Termination Payment). Under the playbook this clause is now acceptable at the fallback; the finding is correctly a deviation against the original text.

Preferred is correctly not claimed: notice stays at 90 days rather than 30, and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is added. If the team wants preferred, it needs a 30-day notice figure in 4.1 plus an express refund sentence (or a recital that fees are payable in arrears so no refund arises).

Drafting defect to repair (not element-fatal): deleting "by either Party hereto" leaves "written notice to the other" without an antecedent. Amend to "...upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party, by the Company for convenience at any time or by HDI only at the end of a term."

Residual readability risk: the Company's right is still delivered inside the auto-renewal sentence in passive voice (which is why the "Customer convenience termination present" regex failed). "for convenience at any time" carries the point, but a standalone sentence — "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice to HDI." — would put the right beyond argument without adding any new obligation.

The HDI prong reads "terminated ... by HDI only at the end of a term" without the words "for convenience", so on a literal reading it could also curtail any HDI termination-for-cause right elsewhere (e.g. Section 1.6). That over-restriction favours us and is not a minimality or intent failure, but insert "for convenience" before "only at the end of a term" if internal consistency with the breach provisions is wanted.

Minimality holds: the original Net Sales computation is retained as prong (i) so no Termination Payment arises at or below $800,000 of trailing Net Sales, 4.2(b)'s zero-or-less netting still operates on the "lesser of" result, and 4.2(c)'s eight quarterly instalments, the Termination Date definition, the one-year term and the auto-renewal structure are untouched. No requirement outside the T4C checklist is added.

Correctly parked in the comment rather than the operative text: that 4.2(a) still bites where the Company terminates for HDI's breach is outside this checklist and should be pursued as a separate ask under the breach/remedies rule.
